mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, increasing real interest rates and eroding real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a rapidly tightening labor market, which increases wage growth and input costs, ultimately producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average AND UNRATE declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average and UNRATE declines.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals strengthening residential demand, which boosts construction-related equities and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months, combined with a flat or declining consumption index (GDPC1), suggests households are saving rather than spending, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months AND GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months and GDPC1 is flat or declining.
